source: Shahjahan, Emmerson & Verstraete, 'On the choice of turbulence model for the simulation of airfoils at Reynolds number below 200,000', ICAS 2024, paper 0327 (file: sa-ai/references/icas2024_0327.pdf)
condition: Eppler 387 airfoil, Re = 200,000, freestream turbulence intensity Tu = 0.1% (paper Sec. 4); incompressible RANS (ANSYS Fluent)
notes: polar: digitized from Figure 6(b), PDF page 10 (Re=200,000 drag polar). The figure is vector art; curve vertex coordinates were extracted programmatically with PyMuPDF get_drawings() and are exactly the per-alpha marker centers (clip-boundary artifacts at the right plot edge removed). Series identified by stroke color matched to legend swatch lines: blue=gamma-Re_theta (Langtry-Menter), green=SA-BC. Axis calibration from tick positions: cd*1e4=0 at px 333.93, tick spacing 24.630 px per 100 (verified against exact vector tick marks); cl=-0.5 at py 695.75, 32.19 px per 0.25 (tick-label centers, verified linear to <0.1 px). x axis is 'Drag coefficient x10^4'; values here are plain cd. Points are in curve (angle-of-attack) order, cl approx -0.3 to 1.26. experiment = wind-tunnel polars (Selig, McGhee, Volkers symbols in the same panel). transition: digitized from Figure 9(a), PDF page 13: TRANSITION location x/c versus angle of attack at Re = 100,000 (NOT 200,000 - Figure 9 is the Re=100k panel; caption symbols identify triangle=transition, circle=laminar separation, square=turbulent reattachment; only the transition triangles are digitized here). experiment_cole = Cole measurements. SA-BC values at alpha=6,7 deg (x/c~0.96) reflect the model's fully-separated state there (no reattachment), as discussed in the paper. transition_re200k: same quantity from Figure 10(a), PDF page 14, at Re = 200,000 (matches the polar condition); experiment = Selig. Transition x/c calibrated from tick-label centers (x/c 0 at px 113.55, 1.0 at 283.7; alpha -2 at py 403.0/192.3, 10 at 281.3/68.75 for p13/p14). Extracted model alphas land on integers to within 0.07 deg, confirming the calibration. All digitization by vector-path extraction, not by eye.
